meaning: Priestly garments and the rebuilding of temple service
description: The number 530 appears in Nehemiah 7:69, where it is stated that the governor gave 530 priestly garments to the treasury as part of the gifts for rebuilding the temple after the Babylonian exile. The priestly robes were essential for restoring the cultic service in Jerusalem, and this gift underscores the strong commitment to renewing the temple service in its full splendor. Beyond this specific occurrence, the number 530 does not have a well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, nor is it linked to any central prophecies or theological concepts that would give it an independent symbolic status.

footnotes.text: The parallel passage in Ezra 2:69 also mentions gifts for temple work but lists 100 priestly garments instead of 530. The difference in numbers between the Ezra and Nehemiah lists is a well-known textual-critical issue that has been discussed by biblical scholars for centuries.

The priestly vestments (Heb. כָּתְנֹת כֹּהֲנִים, kotnot kohanim) were sacred garments that priests had to wear during service in the temple, according to the instructions in Exodus 28–29. Without proper clothing, the priests could not carry out their duties.
